simulations.title: What assistants select in a simulated purchase.
simulations.description: Share of simulated purchases in which each assistant picked the same product.
simulations.caption: {sampleSize} simulated purchases on the same catalog, 2026. Simulated decisions, not live traffic.
simulations.takeaway: Assistants can choose differently. Compare your products across the three models in ecentic’s store scans, then improve the verified data they read.
simulations.pending: The exact Claude and Gemini values, per-model counts and research method are still pending. The approximate 18.5% figure is not plotted as an exact value.

findings.title: What AI agents run into on real stores.
findings.caption: ecentic audits, 2026. Companies are shown without their names. Rows can refer to the same company; each uses its own sample.
findings.note: Every bar shows a failure share. The 88% figure is rounded; an exact faulty-product count was not supplied. These are snapshots, not predicted outcomes for every store.

catalogFaults.label: Products with at least one fault in the data agents read
catalogFaults.detail: A catalog snapshot of the large spirits marketplace.

missingOfferFacts.label: Product pages where an agent found no price, stock or rating
missingOfferFacts.detail: A page sample from the same spirits marketplace.

storeNotNamed.label: Answers that did not name the store for two bottles it stocks
storeNotNamed.detail: The same spirits marketplace was not named in any of the 20 tested answers.

missingDescriptions.label: Listings with no description an agent could use
missingDescriptions.detail: A sample from a flexible workspace network. Publication approval is pending.

paymentBlocked.label: Countries where an agent could not reach payment because of one shipping setting
paymentBlocked.detail: A test of a skincare brand’s checkout in six countries.

findings.roundedDetail: {percentage}% of a {total}-product catalog. The percentage is rounded; the exact faulty-product count was not supplied.

timeline.title: 2026: the rules keep changing.
timeline.caption: Checked {date}. Sources are linked on each event.
timeline.takeaway: Every change can mean new data, new feeds or new checkout rules. Check the current channel requirements before publishing or connecting checkout.

googleUcp.title: Google announces an open standard for agent checkout
googleUcp.detail: The Universal Commerce Protocol connects commerce experiences. Merchant admission and technical requirements remain separate.
googleUcp.source: Google: new agentic commerce tools and protocol

amazonAlexa.title: Amazon combines Rufus and Alexa+ in Alexa for Shopping
amazonAlexa.detail: A shopping assistant on Amazon’s shopping app and website.

metaMuse.title: Meta launches Muse, with approved purchases
metaMuse.detail: Muse can shop using Link checkout and asks for approval before making a purchase.

googleCart.title: Google rolls out Universal Cart in the US
googleCart.detail: Available across Search and Gemini, with Google Pay checkout for supported merchants or a handoff to the merchant’s cart.

shopifyAgentTools.title: Shopify adds agent tools to storefronts and checkout
shopifyAgentTools.detail: WebMCP tools expose shopping operations on Liquid and Hydrogen stores; completing checkout requires buyer approval.

amazonWorkspace.title: Amazon opens the Shop Direct Merchant Workspace
amazonWorkspace.detail: Eligible merchants can register, submit product feeds and manage participation. Shop Direct already existed before this workspace launch.

timeline.pending: Data pending: two additional event dates need readable primary sources before they can be added to this timeline.

channels.title: Every channel has its own way in.
channels.description: Platform buying capability and ecentic integration status are separate. Each channel page explains eligibility and links to the current sources.
channels.caption: Current channel comparison. Last checked {date}.

headers.buying: Can it buy in the answer?

google.reads: Merchant Center catalog data and accurate product pages.
google.buying: Yes, for eligible merchants; Google Pay or merchant-cart handoff.
google.where: Universal Cart: US. Native checkout eligibility includes select merchants in the US, Canada and Australia.

chatgpt.reads: Approved merchant product feeds, listing data and product links.
chatgpt.buying: Approved app/plugin integrations can offer checkout; other links lead to the merchant.
chatgpt.where: Depends on the merchant’s approved integration and supported market.

claude.reads: Product information, plus catalog and checkout tools supplied to a merchant-built agent.
claude.buying: A merchant-built agent can use checkout tools. ecentic has no dedicated Claude checkout connection.
claude.where: Depends on the retailer’s own implementation and tools.

copilot.reads: Web product data and merchant feeds with checkout attributes.
copilot.buying: Copilot Checkout supports eligible purchases in the conversation.
copilot.where: US buyers, USD and English; some onboarding routes remain limited.

perplexity.reads: Product information from merchant websites and shopping results.
perplexity.buying: The documented Buy with Pro flow supports eligible products; other offers link to the store.
perplexity.where: US shopping experience; current merchant access follows the official program.

amazon.reads: Merchant catalogs shared through Shop Direct and its approved routes.
amazon.buying: Eligible Buy for Me purchases; otherwise a link to the merchant’s store.
